public_rationale: A 2023 clinical evaluation, indexed with an April 10, 2024 print publication date, tested GPT-4 on 44 positive-blood-culture cases and reported detailed, well-written responses throughout [e1]. Specialists rated seven management plans harmful, supporting the occasional-dangerous-answer alternative [e2]. A separate study available May 1, 2023 found no majority-rated harmful responses across 66 physician questions; that finding does not negate the harmful responses documented in the clinical evaluation [e3, e2].
limitations: The decisive evaluation concerns bloodstream-infection management and the tested GPT-4 version.
The studies do not establish the frequency of dangerous answers across medical queries generally or explain the difference between their findings.
Clinicians assessed potential harm; actual patient injury was not measured.
The evidence does not establish systematic refusals under aggressive safeguards.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: On medical queries GPT-4 will either refuse (with aggressive guardrails) or occasionally produce plausible but dangerous nonsense.

statement.excerpt: When queried on medicine it will either resist answering (if there are aggressive guardrails) or occasionally spout plausible-sounding but dangerous nonsense.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

from_speaker: occasionally spout plausible-sounding but dangerous nonsense
our_interpretation: The target is the released GPT-4 model, rather than every subsequent model bearing a similar name.
The alternatives concern recurring behavior across medical queries, not a prediction that every answer will be refused or dangerous.
Plausible-sounding but dangerous nonsense means fluent medical recommendations that qualified clinicians identify as incorrect and potentially harmful.
Demonstrating the dangerous-answer alternative does not require establishing that aggressive guardrails were present.
criteria.support_condition: Medical evaluations document fluent GPT-4 answers containing clinically harmful errors, or systematic medical refusals under aggressive safeguards.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative medical evaluations establish that GPT-4 neither systematically refuses under aggressive safeguards nor produces clinically dangerous misinformation. A finite test finding no errors would only bound their frequency.
